key_insight: ARGUS turns long, complex U.S. employment-discrimination complaints into document-level Event Knowledge Graphs, making the underlying legal sequence of actions, actors, timing, and causality easier for AI systems to understand. It combines legal-domain modeling with LLM-based structured generation to produce source-grounded representations instead of relying only on text embeddings.
problem_solved: Employment-discrimination complaints contain multi-step events and relationships that are hard to capture with standard lexical or embedding-based text representations. This paper addresses the need for structured, fact-grounded representations that preserve who did what, when, and why across an entire complaint.
method: Uses a 5W1H-inspired schema to identify key facts from CourtListener complaints.
Extracts fact-bearing statements and builds chunk-level event graphs with participants, temporal links, and causal links.
Combines legal-domain models with LLM-based structured generation to assemble document-level Event Knowledge Graphs (EKGs).
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ARGUS offers a stronger way to model long legal documents where context and sequence matter. It can improve downstream tasks like legal retrieval, case understanding, and structured analysis by preserving source-grounded event structure.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: complaint text -> fact extraction -> chunk-level event graph -> document-level EKG
5W1H wheel or grid showing who, what, when, where, why, and how
Graph visualization with nodes for participants/events and labeled edges for temporal and causal relations
Before-vs-after comparison showing raw text versus structured knowledge graph
paper_title: ARGUS: Role-Aware Event Knowledge Graphs for U.S. Employment-Discrimination Complaints
paper_authors: Sriram Kannan, Swetha Saseendran, Vishnu Vardhan Reddy Kandi, Leslie Barrett, Madhavan Seshadri
